recipes.name: Whole Wheat Blueberry Pancakes
ingredients_raw: 1 cup milk, plus more if necessary

steps.text: Sift flour and baking powder together into a bowl, set aside. Beat milk, egg, artificial sweetener, and salt together in a bowl; stir in flour mixture until just moistened. Add blueberries; stir to combine.

Heat a heavy-bottomed skillet over medium heat; coat with cooking spray. Drop batter by ¼ cupfuls onto skillet and cook until bubbles form, about 1 ½ minutes. Flip and continue cooking until golden brown. Repeat with remaining batter.

raw_recipe.headline: Whole Wheat Blueberry Pancakes
raw_recipe.description: The blueberries in these whole wheat pancakes are so sweet and moist that the pancakes don’t need butter when eaten hot. This recipe makes 10 pancakes.

review.reviewBody: I lost my 100% whole wheat pancake recipe and tried this one. What a wonderful surprise. My son and husband sucked them up and I had to make another batch. I always double it now and use a 1/3 cup batter per pancake. My alterations: All organic ingredients, 3 tablespoons sugar instead of 2, and brown sugar instead of the substitute. Ive made them several times and the recipe proportions are great. As is, you will have a bouncy, very thick pancake. Sometimes the family wants thin pancakes and I add 1/4 cup milk (for base recipe- double this for a double recipe). My recommendation is to use fresh ground flour! Use soft wheat berries. We love this recipe better than my old one!

Wow. Best pancakes i have every made. I usually do not make pancakes because they never turn out . These were perfect. Thick,soft cooked perfect on a cast iron skillet on med /low heat.
I used Spelt and Oat flour,Almond milk,blueberries. A touch of vanilla. Healthy pancakes anyone would eat. 
Will keep this recipe . 
PS. Alea Walt I think you misread the recipe . It is baking powder not baking soda. Might be why it would taste so soapy. That is a lot of soda. 2 tsp.

I'm on a low-sodium, low fat diet. For a single serving, I cut the recipe in half (3/4 c. whole wheat flour, 1 tsp. baking powder) used 1 1/2 Tsp. Egg Beaters, left out the salt and sugar, but added extra blueberries, and a little cinnamon. The batter was thick for pancakes, so I used a little waffle iron. With jelly or maple syrup to sweeten them, they were delicious and heart-healthy. Thanks!

This recipe was pretty good, although I can't say that I adhered to the "healthy" part of it, just the "it tastes wildly good" part.
I did add flax seed like so many reviewers on here mentioned. After that, it was our way......we have a ton of blueberries that I froze this summer (we live in Maine), we also have maple trees that our neighbor "sugars" for us, so fresh maple syrup is always on hand in this house. I have made this a few times now and as the recipes goes it's usually too heavy, so I thin it out with a big splash of buttermilk gently stirred in. I never add sugar because our berries are very sweet and of course so is the syrup. We always make these on an electric griddle and my husband does the honors, he does not use oil or anything else but unsalted butter, so the crispy edges of the pancakes are sheer heaven! This is a great recipe but the photos are awful, I can't imagine why they used old berries for the photoshoot and no syrup, so the pancakes look dried out and unattractive, as a matter of fact so uninteresting it's a wonder anyone tried it! But, I'm glad they did because it drew me in. :-)

Added some extra milk to loosen the batter up and used frozen blueberries, which turned the pancakes a pretty shade of purple. My kids gobbled them up and were very full afterwards - hooray for making our weekend tradition a little healthier! I saved the last portion of batter for me and added some protein powder and they cooked up just as wonderfully. We doubled the recipe, and it gave us 11 pancakes (I used a 1/2-cup scoop to measure each one), which allowed extra to freeze for a quick weekday meal. I will definitely be making these again!!

Okay, this is the first time I have made pancakes that are SO fluffy- but the reason I gave it four stars is that I altered much of the ingredients, which I feel are part responsible for the newfound success: with using normal whole wheat flour, I took out two table spoons and replaced with cornstarch (like cake flour). Then I tripled the amount of baking powder and added lemon extract which reacts well with baking powder. Furthermore, some reviews complain of the dryness so I added one extra egg, two tablespoons of oil, and a tiny bit of extra milk. :) When I put it on the pan, the batter was so thin it spread like a crepe, but then thirty seconds in, the batter suddenly grew upward. Thanks!

I loved these! Very easy. I did not need any extra milk to get the batter to the right consistency. I ended up with four really big pancakes (probably 1/3 to 1/2 cup of batter each), but you would get more if you made regular size pancakes. These are fairly heavy and dense, but I like that and expect it from a whole-wheat pancake. I used blackberries instead of blueberries, and added a little cinnamon. Once I added the batter to the pan, I sprinkled pecans on top so they baked into each pancake and toasted a little once I flipped them. I also added a little wheat germ to the last half of the batter, which added a nice chewy texture. Will definitely make these again!

I tripled this recipe, and put the blueberries on top while cooking the first side and put 1 teaspoon off allspice, cinnamon, and 1/2 a teaspoon of ginger in the batter. [that being the tripled recipe...cut down for single recipes.] A little bit thick even with the added milk, so they were 1/2 an inch thick :P
We loved them! I added shredded coconut, sliced almonds, cinnamon and nutmeg. I also added regular sugar and more blueberries. I cooked them using coconut oil and they were a hit!

I added additional 1/4cup milk, 1 tsp vanilla, 2 tbsp veg. Oil and 1 Tbsp sugar rather than artificial sweetener. They are wonderful. Now I always keep a batch in freezer so I can eat during the week for breakfast. Great recipe whether you have blueberries on hand or not. Wonderful either way. .

I make these all the time for me and my baby! I use agave for the sweetener and only 1 cup flour because I prefer the thinner pancakes. I use almond milk to combat that tree nut allergy. So happy I found this recipe. Thank you!
So fast! So simple! Just YUM 😋 Add a touch more milk for thinner pancakes.
Easy to follow, but the pancakes probably needed more sweetener to stand on their own. Not gonna knock the recipe because I probably screwed that up!

Very good!😋 I tried making these and they turned out great! A bit dense but the blueberries pop in your mouth with each bite! One thing I recommend doing is not mixing the blueberries in with the batter, but pouring your pancake on the pan and adding your blueberries on top!
Super easy to make and fluffy. I’m going to mix 1/2white and 1/2 wheat next time.
Nice recipe! For fluffier pancakes, separate the egg whites and beat them into soft peaks. Then fold that into the batter. This is a keeper..

I must admit I wasn't expecting something that sounds so healthy to taste so good. I used unsweetened almond milk. I just kept pouring until the batter was the right consistency. I will also use a little less sweetener next time. I found 1 tbsp a bit much. Maybe 2 tsp.
Excellent! Light and fluffy.

Its a great base recipe. I like to spice things up a bit. Because its whole wheat, I added some vegetable oil. I've also added sugar, cinnamon, and a splash of amaretto as my flavoring. Adjust to your taste. Then topped it off with some additional blueberries and bananas! Cheers from the Caribbean!

These pancakes were a little on the bitter side for my taste. They are hearty and turn out nice, but the flavor didn't win me over. I think the whole wheat with the 2 tsp of baking powder might be the issue . So as a base recipe I would recommend trying it and tweaking to your preferences. I would suggest adding vanilla and more sugar/sweetener.
